title: A Data-centric Framework to Endow Graph Neural Networks with Out-Of-Distribution Detection Ability

problem.claim: The work addresses OOD detection for graph-structured data at test time.

gap.claim: Existing graph OOD detection methods require training a GNN from scratch, while graph-structured OOD detection remains under-explored.

contributions.claim: AAGOD is a post-hoc, data-centric framework that adds graph OOD detection ability to a well-trained GNN without modifying its parameters.
The framework applies a parameterized amplifier matrix to each input graph's adjacency matrix and reuses the well-trained GNN with scoring functions to produce detection scores.
AAGOD includes a Learnable Amplifier Generator for graph-specific amplifiers and a Regularized Learning Strategy that requires no OOD data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this as the first attempt to endow a well-trained GNN with OOD detection ability without modifying its parameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AAGOD can be applied to various GNNs to enable OOD detection.
Against the stated state-of-the-art graph OOD detection baseline, the authors report average relative improvements of 6.21% in AUC and 34 times faster training.
The authors report that code and data are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: OOD detection is important, but graph-structured OOD detection is under-explored.
Existing graph OOD methods require costly from-scratch GNN training.
AAGOD uses post-hoc adjacency amplification to reuse well-trained GNNs for graph OOD detection.
Graph-specific amplifiers are learned with LAG and RLS without OOD data.
The authors report applicability across GNNs, improved AUC, faster training, and available code and data.

source_observation.claim: A parameterized amplifier is superimposed on each graph's adjacency matrix before encoding by a reused GNN.

interpretation.claim: Input-side or data-centric transformations can extend an existing model's capability without changing model parameters.

application.claim: For deployment settings with costly retraining, consider learning structured input transformations that expose task-relevant patterns to an existing encoder.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach works for all graph tasks, architectures, or deployment conditions.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses a regularized learning strategy without requiring OOD data.

interpretation.claim: Regularization and task-specific objectives may support adaptation when target anomaly examples are unavailable.

application.claim: When labeled OOD examples are unavailable, investigate objectives that learn task-relevant transformations from available data and structural constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, data sources, or failure modes underlying the no-OOD-data training strategy.

unknowns: Datasets, experimental settings, and baseline implementation details are not specified.
The definition and computation of the reported AUC and relative enhancement are not detailed.
The mechanism and objective of the Regularized Learning Strategy are not described.
The scope of applicability across GNN architectures and graph distributions is not established.
